name: Marco Arment
milestone_by_age_26: In 2006–2007, at age 24, co-built Tumblr with David Karp and became its founding lead developer and CTO from launch, helping create one of the defining Web 2.0 microblogging platforms.
early_history_summary: Born June 11, 1982 in Columbus, Ohio; graduated Allegheny College (BS computer science, 2004) and worked as a developer at Vivisimo in Pittsburgh. In 2006 friend David Karp recruited him for a two-week side project that became Tumblr; Arment was first employee/CTO from founding through 2010.
family_context_summary: Born in Columbus, Ohio; mother Catherine later lived in Bexley, Ohio. Broader family financial or professional background not detailed in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: David Karp partnership, Web 2.0 wave, CS degree, NYC tech scene, first-employee equity
evidence_summary: Arment's ≤26 break was technical cofounding of Tumblr at 24 as lead developer/CTO. Path was ordinary CS education plus professional web development rather than elite labs or family tech dynasty. High-trust collaboration with Karp and timing on the microblogging wave were decisive; later solo products (Instapaper, Overcast) confirmed independent product skill.
starting_point: Born 1982 in Columbus, Ohio; raised in Ohio with limited public documentation of family class or professional background; CS graduate of Allegheny College (2004).
current_position: Independent iOS developer and podcaster best known for Overcast; co-hosts Accidental Tech Podcast; lives in the New York area.

trajectory.event: Graduated Allegheny College with a BS in computer science and began professional software work.
Co-built Tumblr with David Karp and joined as founding lead developer/CTO as the platform launched publicly in 2007.
Launched Instapaper, an early successful iPhone read-later app built as a side project while at Tumblr.
Left Tumblr to focus full-time on Instapaper and independent products.
Sold controlling interest in Instapaper to Betaworks.
Released Overcast, a solo-built podcast client that became a long-running category leader on iOS.

name: Anima Patil-Sabale
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Early path was physics/computer applications degrees in Maharashtra and ordinary software engineering jobs in Mumbai then the U.S. (from ~2000); NASA/Kepler and Johnson Space Center roles began around 2012 (~age 38).
early_history_summary: Born in Dhule, Maharashtra, raised in Jalgaon; BSc Physics and MCA at North Maharashtra University; software work in Mumbai then San Jose from March 2000; later MS aerospace (SJSU, 2010) and NASA career.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Indian origin in Maharashtra.
evidence_summary: Career recognition as NASA engineer and astronaut-candidate advocate arrived well after age 26; reviewed sources document standard early software employment rather than a dated breakout by 26.

name: Mike Harrington
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Worked as a programmer at Dynamix (~1985–87) and Microsoft (~1987 onward) as a young adult, but his defining achievement—co-founding Valve with Gabe Newell—was in 1996 at about age 32.
early_history_summary: American programmer who began at Dynamix, spent about nine years at Microsoft (including Windows NT-era work), then left with Newell to found Valve in August 1996; left Valve in 2000 after Half-Life shipped.
evidence_summary: Early industry employment by the mid-20s is documented, but Valve cofounding and Half-Life-era impact came after age 26; no independently dated material breakout ≤26 found.

name: Lilian Weng
milestone_by_age_26: No verifiable material milestone by age 26 found. Public profile centers on later OpenAI research leadership, Lil'Log technical blogging (from 2017), and subsequent Thinking Machines Lab work; birth year is not documented in reviewed sources.
early_history_summary: Educated in China (reports vary between Beihang/Peking University undergrad paths) then U.S. graduate training (CMU/Indiana University mentions in secondary bios); rose as OpenAI research scientist/VP of research & safety before joining Thinking Machines Lab.
evidence_summary: Cannot confirm any specific dated breakout at ≤26 without a birth year; major public AI impact appears mid-career at OpenAI.

name: Nikolai Durov
milestone_by_age_26: In October 2006, at age 25, co-founded VKontakte (VK) with brother Pavel and served as lead developer/CTO of Russia's dominant social network, after already winning three IMO gold medals (1996–98) and two ACM ICPC world titles (2000–01).
early_history_summary: Born November 21, 1980 in Leningrad to philology professor Valery Durov; mathematical prodigy (adult-level reading by 3, cubic equations by 8 per profiles). Dominated IMO/IOI as a teen, won ACM ICPC with St. Petersburg State University, earned PhDs in Arakelov geometry (SPbSU 2005; Bonn under Faltings 2007), and provided the technical core of VK then Telegram (MTProto).
family_context_summary: Father Valery Durov is a Doctor of Philological Sciences and St. Petersburg State University classics/philology professor; academic household in Leningrad/St. Petersburg. Younger brother Pavel became the public face of VK and Telegram.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's domain was classical philology, not software engineering; intellectual/academic orientation is clear, but direct programming apprenticeship is not documented. Sibling partnership with Pavel was the catalytic team structure.
primary_early_advantage_tags: triple IMO gold, IOI medals, ACM ICPC, sibling cofounder Pavel, SPbSU/Bonn math pipeline, VK tech lead
evidence_summary: Nikolai's ≤26 record combines world-class math/programming olympiad dominance from ages 15–21 with co-founding VK as technical lead at 25. Family provided academic stability rather than a software dynasty; brother Pavel supplied product/distribution partnership. Later Telegram protocol work and TON research extended the same scarce systems-math skill stack.
starting_point: Born 1980 in Leningrad into an academic family; father Valery Durov was a university philology professor; raised alongside brother Pavel in St. Petersburg intellectual circles.
current_position: Telegram cofounder and systems architect (MTProto/TON); reclusive mathematician rarely appearing publicly; holds multiple citizenships including Russia.

trajectory.event: Won gold at the International Mathematical Olympiad and gold at the International Olympiad in Informatics.
Completed a three-year run of IMO gold medals (1996–98) plus multiple IOI medals.
Helped Saint Petersburg State University win the ACM ICPC World Finals (repeated in 2001).
Co-founded VKontakte as lead technical developer/CTO as the network launched in October 2006.
Completed a second PhD under Fields Medalist Gerd Faltings at the University of Bonn on singular Arakelov geometry.
Left VK and co-founded Telegram with Pavel, designing the MTProto protocol.
Authored the original Telegram Open Network (TON) whitepaper architecture.

name: Stewart Butterfield
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Earned a BA (1996) and Cambridge MPhil (1998) by his mid-20s; Gradfinder.com (~2000, age ~27), Flickr/Ludicorp (2002, age ~29), and Slack (2013–14) all arrived after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born March 21, 1973 in Lund, BC; early childhood on a commune without running water/electricity; taught himself to code as a child; philosophy degrees then web startups culminating in Flickr and Slack.
family_context_summary: Parents lived on a remote Canadian commune after father avoided the U.S. draft; family moved to Victoria when he was five.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech-industry family; early self-taught coding rather than parental domain transfer.
evidence_summary: Major product outcomes (Flickr, Slack) are post-26; education alone does not meet the material-milestone bar.

name: Shawn Carpenter
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Fame centers on the Titan Rain investigation (from ~2003) while at Sandia National Laboratories and a 2007 wrongful-termination verdict; contemporary reporting put him around age 35 in 2003, well past 26.
early_history_summary: Navy veteran and network security analyst at Sandia who independently tracked Chinese cyberespionage (Titan Rain), collaborated with FBI as informant, was fired in 2005, and later won a multi-million-dollar judgment.
evidence_summary: Defining cybersecurity whistleblowing work is mid-30s; no dated ≤26 material milestone located.

name: Jakob Uszkoreit
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. If born ~1986 (batch metadata), Google internship/hire ~2008 and 2012 search-team work were ordinary early-career roles; the defining 'Attention Is All You Need' Transformer paper arrived in 2017 (~age 31).
early_history_summary: Son of computational linguist Hans Uszkoreit; born while father worked at SRI Menlo Park, raised partly in Germany; university in Berlin, Google internship in translation, full-time Google research career culminating in the 2017 Transformer paper; cofounded Inceptive (2021).
family_context_summary: Father Hans Uszkoreit is a well-known computational linguist; family lived in California when Jakob was born then returned to Germany.
parent_family_domain_summary: Strong parental domain adjacency in computational linguistics/NLP, but the breakout Transformer work came after age 26.
evidence_summary: Field-defining milestone is the 2017 Transformer paper well after 26; early Google employment alone is not treated as a material success-by-26 event.

name: Zach DeVito
milestone_by_age_26: No verifiable material milestone by age 26 found. Known for Stanford PhD work on Terra (dissertation Jan 2015; PLDI 2013) and later PyTorch/TorchScript infrastructure at Facebook/Meta; birth year not documented, so age at those milestones cannot be confirmed ≤26.
early_history_summary: Princeton undergrad, Stanford PhD/postdoc with Pat Hanrahan on high-performance DSLs (Terra, Liszt/Ebb, Darkroom); later FAIR/PyTorch compiler and TorchScript contributor and coauthor on the PyTorch paper ecosystem.
evidence_summary: Strong systems research record exists, but without a birth year the ≤26 eligibility gate cannot be cleared.

name: Eric Niebler
milestone_by_age_26: No verifiable material milestone by age 26 found. Best known for range-v3 and the C++20 std::ranges design (proposals ~2013–2018) and earlier Boost/Microsoft Visual C++ library work; birth year and any dated ≤26 breakout are not documented in reviewed sources.
early_history_summary: Longtime C++ expert, former Microsoft Research / Visual C++ employee and consultant; principal designer behind modern C++ ranges; later work also intersects executors/async and Rust-adjacent systems communities.
evidence_summary: Standards-shaping ranges work is mid/late career; cannot establish age-≤26 material milestone without birth year.

name: Tony Fadell
milestone_by_age_26: In 1995, at age 25–26, was hired by Philips, co-founded its Mobile Computing Group, and became CTO/director of engineering, shipping Windows CE handhelds (Velo/Nino) after three years as a systems architect at Apple spinoff General Magic (from 1992, age 23).
early_history_summary: Born March 22, 1969 in Michigan to a Lebanese father and Polish mother; Grosse Pointe South High School; University of Michigan BS computer engineering 1991, where he ran Constructive Instruments (multimedia software for children) and reportedly started multiple companies before graduating. Early SV path: General Magic → Philips CTO of mobile computing → Fuse → Apple iPod/iPhone leadership → Nest.
family_context_summary: Born in Michigan to a Lebanese-American father and Polish-American mother; specific parental occupations and wealth not detailed in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a consumer-electronics dynasty; Fadell's early product drive appears self-started via college ventures and General Magic immersion.
primary_early_advantage_tags: General Magic, Philips mobile CTO, Michigan CE, Constructive Instruments, handhelds wave
evidence_summary: By 26 Fadell had already progressed from college founder to systems architect at the legendary General Magic and CTO of Philips's mobile computing group shipping real PDA products. That ≤26 operating record—not only later iPod/Nest fame—qualifies him. Advantages were ecosystem immersion and early product reps rather than inherited capital or family domain.
starting_point: Born 1969 in Michigan to a Lebanese father and Polish mother; attended Grosse Pointe South High School and studied computer engineering at the University of Michigan.
current_position: Investor and principal at Build Collective (formerly Future Shape); author of bestseller Build; former Nest CEO and Apple SVP for iPod; splits time internationally including Europe.

trajectory.event: Graduated University of Michigan BS computer engineering after running Constructive Instruments as a student CEO.
Joined Apple spinoff General Magic as diagnostics engineer, rising to systems architect on handheld communicators.
Joined Philips, co-founded Mobile Computing Group, and became CTO/director of engineering for Velo/Nino PDA products.
Joined Apple to lead iPod hardware/software development; first iPod launched October 2001.
Became Senior Vice President of Apple's iPod Division; also contributed to early iPhone generations.
Co-founded Nest Labs with Matt Rogers; Nest Learning Thermostat launched 2011.
Sold Nest to Google for about $3.2 billion; later resigned as Nest CEO in 2016.
Published bestselling book Build: An Unorthodox Guide to Making Things Worth Making.
